_readme: NO-SEED JOURNEY — the shape for a screen fed from a mock or REST source rather than
persisted rows. Reference example for skills/journey-proof.md; tour in
Invented domain: a supplier catalogue browsed through a read-only integration. The
entities behind the grid are non-persistent, so there is no table for OQL to reach.
THE POINT OF THIS FILE IS WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM. Rungs 4 and 5 are structurally
unavailable here, so they are ABSENT AND NAMED AS ABSENT rather than filled with
queries that would return INVALID on every run. A missing rung is `fault`; a fabricated
rung is worse, because it dresses a missing instrument up as coverage.
title: Supplier catalogue — the approver can browse and refresh the integrated catalogue
_seedNote: No seeds, and this is the WHY that an empty array cannot say on its own.
Every entity this journey touches (Procurement.CatalogueEntryReadModel and the four
other read models behind the grid) is NON-PERSISTENT: the list is built in memory by
ACT_Catalogue_Load from a REST call to the upstream system. There is no row to SELECT,
so there is nothing for a {{placeholder}} to bind to and nothing a seed script could
insert that the page would ever show.
This is a different state from 'the seed returned nothing', which is INVALID and means
the fixture or the admin API is broken. An empty seeds[] resolves ok and the walk runs.
Say which of the two you are in — fixture-seeding.md lists four causes of 'seeds return
nothing' with four different owners, and reporting them as one sends someone to debug
_dataRungGap: Every step carries no `data` block, for a measured reason and not by omission:
the module's golden-path data-effects table is empty because this slice is read-only,
and DESCRIBE ENTITY reports every entity in it non-persistent. OQL cannot see a
non-persistent entity, so even a delta check would return null and be recorded INVALID
Record the evidence for the gap in the journey, the way this note does. A reviewer who
sees blank data cells needs to know whether the rung was skipped or was impossible.
_outcomeGap: No `outcome` block. Rung 5 is one OQL query over the end state and there is no end
state in a database to query. The `outcome` control mutant returns false and skips this
journey correctly, so the control run will not fabricate a proof for a rung that cannot
run — it will simply not report one, which is the honest result.
_mutantCoverage: This journey supports four of the seven mutants: ui-landing, ui-text, trace-order and
trace-negative. data-delta, data-target and outcome return false and are skipped.
A green control run over this file proves four rungs, not five. Do not summarise it as

_textAbsentNote: This is the load-bearing check when the data rung is unavailable. The landing guard
goes green on an EMPTY grid — the element renders either way — and the trace rung
goes green because the microflow fires without errors. Reading the rendered text is
the only rung left that can tell a working page from a page showing nothing.
'No items found' is the framework default. If the requirement specifies a designed
empty state, a red here is at minimum a spec miss and possibly two defects stacked:
no rows AND no empty state. Say which you believe it is in the finding, not here.

_note: The negative claim carries real weight on a read-only screen: the requirement says
this path never writes upstream. `mustNotFire` is the only rung that can assert it,
and it is evaluated only because `ordered` is present and non-empty.

actions._note: `wait` takes `ms`; every other action takes `settleMs`, applied after the action.
